leading_positions.synthesis: Four of six round-1 configurations name Drucker, Holst and Mojsov for B006 and frame the prize around the physiology of GLP-1 and the identification of its active form. They share the view that the discovery side should anchor a Physiology or Medicine citation. They differ on how far the citation should acknowledge long-acting analogue development: Perlmann and Linnarsson want the wording to state openly that Knudsen and Habener are not credited, while Sandberg would accept swapping Mojsov for Knudsen if the citation named the therapeutic achievement. The chair is in this group, having moved from his opening trio.

Two of six configurations name Drucker, Holst and Knudsen for B006 and word the citation around physiology plus its development into long-acting incretin therapies. They share the view that the acylated analogues are what made the drug class real. El-Manira stresses that the committee should state its translation principle openly, since it also bears on B004 and B040. Wahren-Herlenius moved off Mojsov in round 1 because naming Mojsov without Habener makes the peptide-identification chapter hard to defend, and she asks that the citation name both physiology and translation.

areas_of_agreement: All six members place B006 (GLP-1 and incretin therapies) as their sole preferred prize part, with Drucker and Holst in every configuration, and none argues that the discovery is premature.
All six name attribution as the main weakness of B006, citing the three-person cap, Habener's absence from the supplied names, and the contested priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide.
Several members (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg) describe B039 (unfolded protein response, Mori and Walter) as having the cleanest attribution on the shortlist.
Members who discuss B028 (cGAS-STING) describe the Chen and Barber mechanism as clean but note that therapeutic translation is not yet established.
Several members (Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius, Linnarsson, Sandberg, Perlmann) flag the Eshhar omission as a problem for any three-name B004 configuration.
Several members state that their accounts of priority are recalled and not verified against primary documents.
scientific_disputes: Whether the B006 prize should centre on discovery of the hormone's physiology and active form (four members) or should also credit the engineering of long-acting analogues (two members), and whether that engineering counts as discovery or as industrial optimisation of an already defined mechanism.

Whether B039 (UPR) should rank ahead of B004 (CAR-T) and B028 (cGAS-STING) given its clean credit but still developing clinical consequence. El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann and Sandberg list B039 as an alternative, while Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius do not.
Whether a mechanism-only recognition is acceptable for B028 given disappointing STING agonist and inhibitor translation, or whether human genetic or clinical evidence is needed first.
Whether the B004 achievement is one line (Rosenberg adoptive transfer, Sadelain costimulated design, June clinical proof of concept) or distinct achievements, as Wahren-Herlenius questions.
attribution_disputes: Third GLP-1 name: Mojsov (Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson) versus Knudsen (El-Manira, Wahren-Herlenius). The two configurations differ only in this name, and the citations differ accordingly.

Habener is outside the supplied B006 names but is cited by members on both sides as part of the active-peptide record, and Mojsov's priority is described as contested. Several members say it cannot be settled from the ballots.
B004: Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited names, and members differ on whether Rosenberg belongs alongside June and Sadelain (Linnarsson proposes only June and Sadelain).
B037: the six credited names are not narrowed to three in any configuration, and the chair noted this as open.
B039: Linnarsson and Sandberg note that Ron, Kaufman and Kozutsumi, and the other UPR arms (PERK, ATF6), are not trivially excluded despite the otherwise compact Mori and Walter attribution.
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B006. Perlmann notes that long-term safety data are still accumulating, and Wahren-Herlenius notes that the clinical field continues to move.
B039 is described as having two decades of stable attribution but still-early therapeutic payoff (ISRIB, PERK inhibitors), so members differ on whether fundamental-mechanism maturity is sufficient.
B028 is described as a candidate for a later year because no validated therapy exists, while Wahren-Herlenius argues its mechanistic clarity deserves a higher position.
B004 clinical maturity is described as complete, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, but attribution rather than maturity is its limiting issue.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) disclosed about twenty co-authored works with fellow member Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. No shortlisted credited name is linked, and he offered to accept recusal guidance if a neuroscience candidate such as B037 became the leading choice.

El-Manira disclosed a 2009 paper with Perlmann, a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, and work with Patrik Ernfors. None involves a shortlisted candidate. B037 is in his own field but he lists no personal tie to its candidates.
Sandberg and Linnarsson disclosed co-authorship with each other and with Jonas Frisen, with no link to any shortlisted candidate or credited name.
Perlmann disclosed a nuclear-receptor collaboration with Ronald Evans, work with Johan Ericson, and co-authorship with committee colleagues, none involving a shortlisted candidate.
Wahren-Herlenius notes that B028 and autoimmunity candidates are near her field but discloses no personal or institutional connection to any shortlisted candidate.
questions_for_round2: For B006, should the third name be Mojsov or Knudsen, and what documentary evidence on the Mojsov and Habener priority question for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is available to the committee?

Should the B006 citation be framed around physiology and the active peptide, or around physiology plus long-acting therapy development, and how should it acknowledge whichever contributors are omitted?
If translation or industrial development may be credited in B006, will the committee apply the same principle to B004 and B040, and if not, what distinguishes them?
Is the committee prepared to consider a second prize part, for example B039, B004 or B028, given that B006 already uses three names, and which B006 name would be dropped?
For B004, can the committee settle Eshhar's omission and whether Rosenberg belongs with June and Sadelain, before treating it as an alternative?
If a neuroscience candidate such as B037 becomes a leading option, how should the disclosed Svenningsson-Perlmann co-authorship and El-Manira's field overlap be handled?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows unanimous placement of B006 with a clear 4-2 split on the third laureate, and no other ballot appears in any member's preferred configuration. The split reflects a principled difference about discovery versus translation and not about scientific merit or maturity. Alternatives are dispersed: B004 appears in five members' alternatives, B039 in four, B037 in two and B028 in one. Round 2 should resolve the third name and citation wording for B006 before deciding whether any second prize part is warranted.
